_comment: Cross-language contract for Kafka topic naming. THREE implementations must
agree on this table:
- shared/go/kafkaclient/topics.go            (orchestrator, api-gateway, adapter, sink)
- llm-service/src/utils/kafka_topics.py      (planner, PII scanner)
- shared/mcp-connectors/internal/debezium/versions/v1.0.0/connector.py
They are separate copies because they ship in different images with
different paths. A divergence between them does not raise: the producer
writes one name, the consumer subscribes to another, and the pipeline
simply goes quiet. Each language's test suite reads this file, so drifting
one implementation reddens that language's build.
Adding a case here is the intended way to pin new behavior.
The rsync.-spelled inputs below are the ones worth reading twice. Four topics
spell the product name in the literal itself (rsync.notifications,
rsync.healer.{results,approved-changes,schema-changes}). At the default
prefix, qualifying one is a no-op -- it already starts with rsync. -- so a call
site that forgot to qualify is indistinguishable from one that did. Under a
customer prefix the two diverge: acme.rsync.notifications vs rsync.notifications.
That is a real production defect (see api-gateway notifier + schema_evolution),
and it is invisible to every test that runs at the default prefix, so the
custom-prefix rows are pinned here rather than left to each implementation.
